text:
oliver: quick summary from today's long-context quant run (24k/64k sweep) — put together SmoothQuant + activation-aware quant variants against fp16 baseline. saw some interesting tradeoffs, posting numbers and recommendations. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
maya: awesome, want the quick delta numbers pls — both quality and mem/latency
oliver: short table (aggregate over 3 seeds):
```
model: redwood-13B-v2
baseline fp16: ppl 12.3 | EM 0.82 | avg latency 210ms | mem 12.1GB
sq int8 (smoothquant act-aware): ppl 12.9 (+4.9%) | EM 0.79 | latency 165ms | mem 8.9GB
awq-hybrid (layerwise act-scale + int8 weights): ppl 12.5 (+1.6%) | EM 0.80 | latency 150ms | mem 9.3GB
gptq (static): ppl 13.7 (+11.4%) | EM 0.76 | latency 140ms | mem 7.8GB
```
oliver: key notes: AWQ-hybrid gives best overall latency but a small quality hit (~1.6% ppl). GPTQ gave lowest mem but worst quality on instruction-heavy evals. SQ-int8 is a decent middle ground.

kai: what about long-kv behavior? any evictions or mismatch patterns at 64k?
oliver: yes — AWQ introduces per-layer scaling tables that increase KV cache growth ~+12% vs fp16 on our runtime, so on constrained buckets we saw earlier eviction at ~52k instead of 60k. SQ kept KV growth similar to fp16.

sam: any patterns in where errors show up? (token types, instruction vs narrative)
oliver: errors clustered on multi-step instruction chains and math reasoning. hallucination rate up slightly in GPTQ, AWQ had more soft-token probs (more low-confidence tokens), SQ mistakes were more local and often recoverable.

maya: can you paste the quant command flags you used?
oliver: sure:
```bash
python tools/quantize.py --model redwood-13B-v2 --algo smoothquant --bits 8 --act-aware --calib-dset eval_small.json --seed 42
python tools/quantize.py --model redwood-13B-v2 --algo awq --bits 8 --hybrid_layers "0,1,2,6,7" --calib 2048
```
oliver: calibration used 2k samples sampled from instruction-rich eval set. eval harness: 5k prompts including longchain, math, code.

tess: recommend we do two things: 1) run a focused prompt-level regression set (100 prompts) to capture where AWQ fails, 2) run a 48h canary on a dedicated pool with fallback-to-fp16 on mismatch threshold 0.12 (per-token KL).

sam: +1. I'll allocate a Dedicated small pool (pool-3) and route 8% traffic for 24h then 48h if stable. Can we automate fallback?

oliver: yes — runtime supports per-request fallback when top-k disagreement > threshold. quick pseudocode in runtime hooks: 
```python
if kl(topk(fp16), topk(quant)) > 0.12:
  route_to(fp16_model)
else:
  serve(quant_model)
```

kai: any perf regressions in batching/throughput?
oliver: AWQ has slightly better single-request latency but under heavy batching we measured ~10% reduced throughput vs SQ because of layer scaling table lookups. net cost savings still positive for AWQ due to lower token compute.

maya: what's the recommendation for rollout?
maya: (1) canary AWQ-hybrid on non-critical routes w/ fallback, (2) keep SQ-int8 for high-reliability low-drift routes, (3) GPTQ only if mem is the primary constraint and quality is acceptable for that customer.

sam: I'll schedule canary tonight at 22:30 PT. @deploy-bot start canary when ready.

deploy-bot: canary job submitted -> dedicated/pool-3 -> config: model=redwood-13B-v2-awq-hybrid, traffic=8%, fallback_threshold=0.12, duration=48h

tess: tagging this for QA: please run the 100-prompt regression set after 6h and at 24h. ping @maya for eval review.

oliver: noted — I'll push the full logs and eval artifacts to /mnt/evals/2026-03-awq-sq-longctx in 30m. seed=42 included.

maya: thanks — let's re-run with calibrationsize=4096 if we see >2% drift at 24h.

sam: moving to action. will post canary link and perf dashboard when live. :rocket:
